newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Saab Aircraft sees its market improving.
newsitem.headline: Saab Aircraft sees its market improving.

text.p: Saab Aircraft sees markets improving for both its Saab 340 and Saab 2000 civilian aircraft models, the company's information director Anders Annerfalk told Reuters.
"We know that the market for new passenger aircraft is growing. It is happening slowly, but the trend is clear - orders are on the increase," Annerfalk said.
Saab AB said in its nine-month results report on Monday that production of the two aircraft was loss-making.
More than 400 of the Saab 340's have now been produced and have now found an opening in the all-important U.S. market.

"The U.S. civil aviation authority has stepped up safety requirements for planes in the size category below the 340 which makes them more costly to operate. Companies which are on the borderline have an incentive to go up a class and we have already noticed more enquiries," Annerfalk said.
Saab is now waiting for the second wave of orders to arrive for its newer Saab 2000.
Fifty of the planes have been sold since its launch three years ago and 40 of these have been delivered.
"We have noticed that those companies which were hesitant at the launch are again showing interest," he said.
Annerfalk said Saab 2000 had now been in service with some airlines for two years, which gave it the advantage of providing realistic operating cost data.
Saab believes it can sell the plane on the basis of the data.
